[Blog] [Cookbook] About SGLang-Omni is a multi-stage serving runtime for omni, speech, and TTS models. Its design target is multi-stage decoding: generation split across heterogeneous stages with different compute patterns, dependency structures, and resource needs. SGLang-Omni owns the pipeline topology, stage lifecycle, inter-stage transport, model-family integration layer, and OpenAI-compatible serving surface, while composing with SGLang for high-performance autoregressive scheduling and model execution where applicable. Multi-stage runtime: SGLang-Omni models generation as coordinated stages: preprocessing, encoders, autoregressive engines, talkers, decoders, vocoders, and aggregators. Stage-specialized scheduling: Each stage runs behind a scheduler matched to its workload, from SGLang-backed autoregressive scheduling to lightweight preprocessing and streaming vocoder loops. Transport-aware execution: A control plane coordinates requests while the relay data plane moves tensor payloads across shared-memory, NCCL, NIXL, and Mooncake backends. API surface: OpenAI-compatible endpoints expose multimodal chat, speech generation, batch speech, streaming speech, uploaded voices, and transcription. What SGLang-Omni Serves Omni chat and speech: Qwen3-Omni, MiniCPM-o 4.5, Ming-Omni, Ming-3.0-audio-flash — multimodal understanding and text/audio replies. Native full-duplex conversation: MiniCPM-o 4.5, PersonaPlex, NemotronLabs VoiceChat — live listening and speaking over /v1/realtime, including camera input with MiniCPM-o. Full-duplex guide. Cascaded voice assistants: Compose ASR → LLM → TTS services into streaming, turn-based conversations with voice activity detection, conversation history, turn taking, and interruption. Streaming cascade guide. Image and video generation: LLaDA2.0-Uni for text/image understanding, image generation, and editing; Cosmos3 Nano for interleaved understanding and generation, with native image, video, and action routes. Music generation: MiniMax Music 3 — lyrics + caption → 32 kHz stereo song. Speech generation: Higgs Audio v3, MOSS-TTS, MOSS-TTS Local, Fish Audio Drama 3, Fish Speech S2-Pro, Qwen3-TTS, Fun-CosyVoice3, Voxtral TTS, Ming-Omni-TTS, Ming-3.0-TTS, dots.tts, ZONOS2 — /v1/audio/speech, with batch, streaming, and voice features varying by model. Instruction-driven speech generation and editing: AuK and AuK-Flash — text and voice instructions → speech; audio and editing instructions → edited speech. Audio transcription: Qwen3-ASR, Fun-ASR, ARK-ASR, Nemotron 3.5 ASR, Nemotron Transcribe, Ming-3.0-ASR, experimental Whisper, and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize via /v1/audio/transcriptions. MOSS-TD also returns speaker labels and timestamps (response_format=verbose_json). Speaker diarization: Nemotron 3 Diarization — speaker intervals for uploaded recordings and live audio, including overlapping speech. Speech translation: Hy-SimulMT — Chinese speech → English text and English speech → Chinese text, with file and realtime translation. See the audio translation guide for endpoint and model support. Hardware Support Backend Status Notes NVIDIA CUDA Supported Default backend with full model coverage. Apple Silicon Experimental Qwen3-ASR runs through Torch MPS on macOS arm64. Install with install.sh and follow the Qwen3-ASR guide. Intel GPU (XPU) Supported Intel Arc GPUs via PyTorch XPU. Qwen3-ASR, Whisper ASR, Fun-ASR-Nano, Nemotron 3.5 ASR, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, Qwen3-TTS, Fun-CosyVoice3, ZONOS2, Audar-TTS, Qwen3-Omni, MiniMax Music 3, MiniCPM-o, Ming-Omni, Ming-Omni-TTS, Nemotron VoiceChat, PersonaPlex, AuK/AuK-Flash and dots.tts serve end-to-end. The Intel XPU guide has the install steps, each model's launch command and how many cards it needs; the backend is auto-detected. Additional model guides, including experimental and research-oriented paths, are available in the Cookbook. Quick Start Installation TTS usage ASR cookbook Community & Support SGLang-Omni welcomes contributors working on inference systems, kernels, scheduling, inter-stage communication, model runners and cache efficiency, model integration, benchmarking, production deployment. Join the SGLang Slack or read the developer reference. Organizations interested in supporting SGLang-Omni, TTS, or omni model serving can contact Chenyang Zhao at zhaochenyang@lmsys.org.
